input: Re-examining my recommendation after resolving the obligation I had left open. The decisive fact: Vendor B processes and stores all data in the United States only, with EU in-region residency not available until a roadmap target of Q3 2027 — yet Meridian has publicly and contractually committed to its EU customers (in the Data Processing Agreement and on its public security page) that their data is processed and stored within the EU, and EU customers are ~35% of ARR. Migrating ~2.4M PII records including EU data subjects to Vendor B would breach that commitment. The $32k three-year saving is a preferred indifferent and does not outweigh the obligation to keep faith with EU customers. I therefore now lean: do NOT recommend the migration to Vendor B as proposed; keep EU customer data on EU-resident infrastructure (retain Vendor A for now), and revisit Vendor B only if it can contractually guarantee EU in-region data residency. Is this corrected judgement sound?

prior_feedback.adopted_correction: Resolved the previously-unevaluated obligation to the EU-customer circle: Vendor B US-only hosting breaches Meridian public EU data-residency commitment, so the cost saving (a preferred indifferent) does not justify proceeding.
